sheet-2-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 2 is the main map of the sheet, covering the northern end of Hackettstown east of Main Street between the farm land beyond Prospect Avenue and Railroad Avenue with the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) along the bottom edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, and Main Street runs down the left edge. Blocks 83, 84 and 15 are numbered. The upper half is residential: frame dwellings, most of two and a half storeys, face Main Street and Prospect Avenue, with a few brick houses on Prospect Avenue and long narrow lots running back towards open land. At the top left are the small brook, a drive and the house of Willow Brook Farm (Klotz and Ackley, proprietors), whose farm buildings are drawn in an inset in the upper right corner. The lower half is industrial. Along Stiger Street and Railroad Avenue stand the large works of the American Saw Mill Machinery Co.: a machine shop, assembling, casting and storage buildings, a covered shipping platform, a foundry, pattern storage, a flask shed, cleaning and casting rooms, an engine house and a wood working shop, much of it of brick. The American Saw Works occupies the corner of Main and Stiger Streets, with lumber sheds and small shops. To the east lies an open Base Ball Ground. Water pipes run along Main Street, Prospect Avenue, Stiger Street and Railroad Avenue. The heavy box in the upper right encloses the inset, part 2 of the sheet.
notes: Prospect Avenue and Stiger are East Prospect Street and East Stiger Street in OpenStreetMap.
Railroad Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Works of the American Saw Mill Machinery Co. between Stiger Street and Railroad Avenue.
Placed from two junctions on Main Street and the railroad crossing (helmert).
50 ft. North Main Street: Prospect Av, Stiger, Railroad Av, American Saw Mill Machinery Co. Two parts: 1 main; 2 inset top right (Willow Brook Farm, Klotz & Ackley), no street junction.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Willow Brook Farm (Klotz & Ackley), farm buildings in block 83 (no street junction; only a farm lane and a small brook; needs hand-picked control (parcel corners) if the farm can be located).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the northern end of Hackettstown's downtown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Main Street runs up the sheet from the bottom edge, where it meets Grand Avenue and High Street, to the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western railroad yard at the top, where the tracks cross it. Valentine Street and Liberty Street run east from Main Street and Washington Street runs down the left side. Cutler Street, labelled Depot Park, and Railroad Avenue lie along the tracks. The railroad corridor across the upper part of the sheet holds the passenger station, a freight depot, a coal yard and the sidings, with Smith Bros and Co., contractors, and a second coal yard at the top. Below the tracks the blocks hold dwellings on the west side and mixed commerce along Main Street: a large garage with room for fifty cars, a ladies' underwear factory (Rosenstock and Cohn), a plumbing shop, the Hoffman House, the American House hotel, a bank, a public library, a hotel garage and a gasoline station. A lumber and builders' materials yard (Williams and Hibler) fills the right-hand edge near Liberty Street. Franklin Street is lettered on the right margin and Stiger Street at the top. The compass rose near the railroad is turned with the sheet. Neighbouring sheets are 5 above, 2 and 4 to the right, 7 below left and 8 below.
notes: Cutler Street (lettered 'Depot Park') and Railroad Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap today and were not used as control.

Main Street, High Street and Grand Avenue meet at one modern node (Grand Avenue / Main Street); the sheet draws Grand Avenue meeting Main Street about 20 m north of High Street, and the detected junction is the Grand Avenue one.
Main Street / Liberty Street was placed by hand; the detector did not find it.
50 ft. Downtown north: Main, Railroad Av, Valentine, Liberty, High, Washington, Cutler, D.L.&W. station. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the north-eastern residential blocks of Hackettstown at 50 feet to an inch. North lies towards the upper left, so Liberty, High, Sharp and Lafayette Streets run down the sheet to the lower right and Cook Street and Franklin Street cross them. Railroad Avenue runs down the left margin beside the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western tracks, where a milk company plant (J. C. Welsh Milk Co.) and a coal and lumber yard (Williams and Hibler) stand at the edges. The remainder of the sheet is detached frame dwellings on regular lots with outbuildings and a few stables or garages. A Roman Catholic church stands on the block between Cook Street and Liberty Street at the upper left, and a few other small public or institutional buildings are coloured blue or pink. Block numbers 30, 31, 11, 14, 212, 215 and 401 are printed in the blocks. A compass rose at the right edge shows the turned orientation. The sheet has a lot of blank ground between the dwellings and a few outlying houses along Lafayette Street at the upper right. Neighbouring sheets are 2 and 3 to the left, 5 to the right and 8 below.
notes: Cook Street is lettered twice, on both sides of the High Street block, and is one street.
Liberty Street here runs down the sheet while on sheet 3 it runs east from Main Street; the sheets are turned differently (this one about 115 degrees from sheet 3).
Cook Street / Liberty Street, Cook Street / Lafayette Street and Franklin Street / Lafayette Street were not detected.
50 ft. North-east: High, Cook, Sharp, Franklin, Liberty, Lafayette. One part.

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 is the western strip of the sheet, showing Grand Avenue on the western edge of Hackettstown between 1st Avenue at the top and the vacant land beyond 3rd Avenue at the bottom, with the double-track Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) running down the left side. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that Grand Avenue runs down the page and north lies towards the upper left. Most of the part is open land: blocks 51, 82, 209 and 208 hold only a few frame dwellings, barns and poultry houses along Grand Avenue, and a dismantled windmill is noted. The dominant feature is The Lackawanna Leather Co., manufacturers of automobile, carriage and furniture leather, on block 201 between 3rd Avenue, Grand Avenue and the railroad: a group of brick buildings for tanning, japanning, splitting, retanning, graining and storage, a hide house, a beam house, a repair and machine shop with engine and boiler rooms, coal sheds, a reinforced-concrete warehouse built in 1916, an office and a 30,000 gallon elevated sprinkler tank, with a printed note on the plant's fire protection. West of the railroad lie a Standard Oil Co. of N.J. storage plant with iron gasoline and kerosene tanks, settling ponds for waste water, and vacant land in blocks 199 and 200. A proposed extension of 1st Avenue is drawn at the top left. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn along Grand Avenue. The part is separated from parts 2 and 3 by a heavy line.
notes: 3rd Avenue is drawn north of Grand Avenue, between Grand Avenue and the railroad; in OpenStreetMap 3rd Avenue meets Grand Avenue only from the south.

The fit through 1st Avenue and 3rd Avenue at Grand Avenue gives about 7.4 px/ft against 8.15 on the other sheets: this part appears drawn about 9 percent small; modern lot lines along Grand Avenue agree with the placement.
The Lackawanna Leather Co. plant fills block 201.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 west Grand Av / 3rd Av / 1st Av with Lackawanna Leather Co. and the D.L.&W. railroad (left); 2 Maple Av / Lafayette / Sharp / Franklin, W.H. Ashley Silk Corp. (upper right); 3 Cutler Street by the railroad, Harvey & Cole coal, N.J. Power & Light (lower right).

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 is the upper right of the sheet, in the north-eastern part of Hackettstown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies roughly to the right. It shows the blocks between Sharp Street at the top and Lafayette Street, with Franklin Street along the right edge and Maple Avenue running diagonally up the lower left. Block 213, between Sharp and Lafayette, is a row of small frame dwellings: about a dozen two-and-a-half storey houses on narrow lots facing Lafayette Street (numbers 100 to 116) and larger houses facing Sharp Street, with stables and garages at the rear. The area south of Lafayette is block 86, largely open, crossed by a brook with an iron bridge at Franklin Street and a wooden bridge at Maple Avenue. The main building there is the W. H. Ashley Silk Corpn., silk throwsters: a brick mill with a dye house of concrete, a machine shop, an engine and boiler house and a box storage shed, with a note on its watchman, heating, lighting and hydrant connected to the town water. A narrow strip marked no exposure lies along the heavy line on the left, which separates this part from part 1. Water pipes of 2, 3 and 4 inches run along Sharp, Lafayette and Franklin Streets. The sheet title box sits in block 213.
notes: W. H. Ashley Silk Corporation silk throwing mill on block 86.
Placed from three junctions (an exact fit); modern parcel lines in block 213 agree with the placement.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 west Grand Av / 3rd Av / 1st Av with Lackawanna Leather Co. and the D.L.&W. railroad (left); 2 Maple Av / Lafayette / Sharp / Franklin, W.H. Ashley Silk Corp. (upper right); 3 Cutler Street by the railroad, Harvey & Cole coal, N.J. Power & Light (lower right).

sheet-5-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 5 is the lower right of the sheet, a small area beside the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) near the Hackettstown station, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The railroad's tracks and sidings run down the middle of the part. To their left, in block 16 along a vacant field, are the coal yard of Harvey S. Cole, with a frame bunk house, coal sheds and a section house, and the plant of the New Jersey Power & Light Co., heated by steam and lit by electricity, with its engine house, generators, soft coal bin and a coal elevator. A long frame building on the right, in block 3, stands beside the tracks. Cutler Street runs up the right side of the part and is lettered a second time along the bottom, marked to be closed; an auto painting shop and two small buildings stand on its far side, with vacant fields beyond. The heavy line along the top and left separates this part from parts 1 and 2 of the sheet; sheet 13 adjoins at the upper right and block 206 lies at the bottom.
notes: Cutler Street is marked 'to be closed' and is not in OpenStreetMap today.
New Jersey Power & Light Co. plant and Harvey S. Cole coal yard on block 16.

Placed from two corners of the long building by the passenger station that sheet 3 draws in full (carried from sheet 3), with the scale assumed and north set from the drawn tracks against the modern railroad (the arrow suggests about 9 degrees more); low confidence.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 west Grand Av / 3rd Av / 1st Av with Lackawanna Leather Co. and the D.L.&W. railroad (left); 2 Maple Av / Lafayette / Sharp / Franklin, W.H. Ashley Silk Corp. (upper right); 3 Cutler Street by the railroad, Harvey & Cole coal, N.J. Power & Light (lower right).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the western edge of Hackettstown at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. Grand Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet and Moore Street crosses the middle, both running east-west. Beatty Street runs between them, 1st Avenue slants across the left side, Jefferson Street forms the right margin and West Plane Street the bottom edge. The upper blocks between Grand Avenue and Moore Street hold detached dwellings with a few small outbuildings, mostly on the west side of Beatty Street, and the north side of Grand Avenue shows vacant fields, sheds and a few houses. The lower half is occupied by the grounds of the Centenary Collegiate Institute of the Newark M.E. Conference for Girls, drawn in colour: North Hall and South Hall dormitories joined by curved drives, an administration building, chemical and physical laboratories, a gymnasium with swimming pool, and bowling alleys, all heated by steam and lit by electricity. Large parts of the grounds are left blank and lettered as the C.C.I. property. Cutler's Lane runs northeast at the top. A compass rose stands at the upper left. The blank areas at the left and bottom belong to the neighbouring sheets 5, 7 and 12.
notes: Moore is Moore Street in OpenStreetMap; West Plane is Plane Street.
The sheet letters a 'Proposed Extension of Beatty St.' north of Grand Avenue and a 'Proposed Extension of First Av.' off the left edge; neither is built as drawn.
Jefferson Street / Plane Street was placed by hand at the bottom right.
50 ft. West: Grand Av, Moore, W. Plane, Beatty, Jefferson, Centenary Collegiate Institute. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers six residential blocks in the western part of Hackettstown, west of the downtown. It is bounded by Grand Avenue at the top, West Plane Street at the bottom, Jefferson Street on the left edge and Madison Street towards the right, with Moore Street and Church Street running across the middle and Monroe Street running down the centre of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. The blocks are numbered 52, 53, 56, 38, 54, 55, 9, 33 and 34 in the key map's sequence. The district is almost entirely residential: rows of detached frame dwellings, most of two or two and a half storeys, set back on deep lots, with stables and small outbuildings at the rear of many lots. There are very few commercial or industrial buildings; a small print shop stands on Grand Avenue near the west end, and one concrete-block or brick-veneered building appears in block 53. North of Grand Avenue the sheet shows the edge of block 205, marked as a vacant field, with Cutler Street drawn running north from Grand Avenue and annotated as to be closed. Water pipes, mostly of 3 and 4 inches, are drawn along Grand Avenue, Moore Street, Church Street and the cross streets, with fire hydrants at several corners. Street widths are lettered at a few points (66 feet on Jefferson Street and 68 feet on Cutler Street). The neighbouring sheets are 6 to the west, 8 to the east, 3 to the north and 12 to the south.
notes: Cutler Street, north of Grand Avenue, is marked 'to be closed'; it is not in OpenStreetMap today.
Moore and West Plane are Moore Street and Plane Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Grand Av, Moore, Church, W. Plane between Jefferson, Monroe and Madison. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the core of Hackettstown's downtown at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. Main Street runs down the right-centre of the sheet, Washington Street down the left, and Grand Avenue, Moore Street, Church Street and West Plane Street cross them. The block along Grand Avenue holds the Hotel Clarendon, and a hotel garage; Moore Street and Main Street carry the commercial frontage, including the Strand Theatre, the Hackettstown Steam Laundry and the Post Office. A Town Hall with a fire company house stands on the block between Moore and Church Streets west of Main Street. Churches include St. James Episcopal Church at the left edge and Trinity M.E. Church with its chapel on the east side of Main Street, and a large garage with a cement floor fills a block near West Plane Street. East of Main Street the blocks are mostly dwellings, and the diagonal streets at the top right are High Street and Sharp Street, which belong to the neighbouring sheet 4. Block numbers 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 33 and 34 are printed on the sheet. Water pipes are drawn in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. A compass rose is on the east side. The sheet adjoins sheets 3 above, 7 to the left, 9 below and 4 to the upper right.
notes: Moore is Moore Street west of Washington Street and West Moore Street between Washington and Main in OpenStreetMap; West Plane is Plane Street; East Plane is East Plane Street.
Main Street / Plane Street and Grand Avenue / Main Street were not detected.
50 ft. Downtown: Grand Av, Moore, Church, W. Plane, Washington, Main. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the southern part of Hackettstown's downtown at 50 feet to an inch. Main Street runs down the middle, Washington Street runs down the left margin, and West Plane Street (left) and East Plane Street (right) cross the top, with Center Street and Warren Street crossing lower down. Willow Grove runs diagonally up to the right across the bottom right corner. West of Main Street the blocks are detached dwellings, many with rear stables, and the First Presbyterian Church stands near the middle of the block between Center and Warren Streets. Main Street carries commercial buildings: the Central Hotel and a garage with a cement floor at the top right, a knitting mill (Swiss Knitting Co.) and several shops. The Presbyterian Sunday School and a large Grave Yard lie east of Main Street in the centre. A stream with a bridge runs down the upper right corner. The compass rose at the right is turned with the sheet. Water pipes with hydrants are drawn in the streets. Neighbouring sheets are 8 above, 10 below, 11 to the right and 12 to the left.
notes: West Plane is Plane Street and East Plane is East Plane Street in OpenStreetMap; Main Street / East Plane Street and Main Street / Willow Grove Street were not detected.
Willow Grove meets Main Street about 18 m south of Warren Street; the modern node shows the two within 15 m.
50 ft. W./E. Plane, Center, Warren, Washington, Main, Willow Grove. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the south-western edge of Hackettstown at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the top of the sheet. Mountain Avenue runs down the middle from the junction of Main Street, Mill Street and Willow Grove Street at the top to Bells Lane at the bottom, and Washington Street runs down the left margin. Warren Street comes in from the top left, Mill Street runs southeast from Main Street, Little Street crosses the middle, and Water Street appears twice: as a street running down the right side and as a diagonal across the lower middle. The district is residential, with detached dwellings along Mountain Avenue and Water Street, a garage at the top beside Willow Grove Street, and a number of long narrow lots between the streets. The right edge shows the Musconetcong River winding down the sheet with a block of dwellings on its bank. The lower part of the sheet is open ground and large lots. Block numbers 9, 17, 18, 19, 20, 59, 106, 12 and 404 are printed. A compass rose with a vertical north arrow stands at the upper left. Neighbouring sheets are 9 above, 11 to the right and 12 below.
notes: Main Street, Mill Street and Mountain Avenue meet at one modern node; the sheet draws them meeting at the top between Main Street and Willow Grove Street.
Mountain Avenue / Water Street and Bells Lane / Mountain Avenue were placed by hand.
Mill Street / Water Street was measured from a narrow pair of edges (40 of 60 ft).
50 ft. South: Washington, Mountain Av, Warren, Water, Little; Musconetcong River. One part.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 is an L-shaped area on the south side of Hackettstown: a strip along Mountain Avenue on the left of the sheet, joined at the bottom to East Avenue, here also called Crane, and to the river crossing in the lower right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. Mountain Avenue, numbered 158 to 201, is lined on both sides with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys on deep lots, with barns and stables at the rear; the Musconetcong River winds down the right side of the strip beside a vacant strip of block 107. At the bottom, East Avenue runs east from Mountain Avenue past a few dwellings to the Musconetcong River, where the Warren Berry grist mill stands beside a dam, a tail race and a feed storage building, and an iron bridge carries the road across the river. Beyond the river East Avenue turns north-east past the Union Cemetery, whose tool house and stable are drawn, and the county line between Warren and Morris Counties follows the river. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed in the open land of block 107. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Mountain Avenue and East Avenue. The heavy lines enclose parts 2, 3 and 4 of the sheet, which show other areas of the town.
notes: East Avenue is lettered 'East Av. (Crane)': Crane is an older name ('Crane, see East Ave.' in the index).
Warren Berry grist mill on the Musconetcong River at East Avenue.
Placed from one junction (Mountain Avenue / East Avenue) with the scale assumed and rotation from its drawn lines; the modern line of East Avenue follows the drawn road through the river crossing.

50 ft. Four parts: 1 Mountain Av and East Av (Crane) along the Musconetcong River (left strip and bottom); 2 Miller St / Sharp / Lafayette, turned about 90 degrees (central box); 3 Mill Pond, Mill St, Gruendyke grist mill (top); 4 Willow Grove / Maple Av, M.B. Bowers implements (right middle).

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is the pentagonal area enclosed by heavy lines in the middle of the sheet, showing Miller Street between Sharp Street and Lafayette Street in the north-eastern part of Hackettstown. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north to the right, so that Sharp and Lafayette Streets run across the sheet and Miller Street runs down it. Block 101 lies above Sharp Street, block 401 between Sharp and Lafayette, and block 215 below Lafayette; blocks 211 and 216 lie on the far side of Miller Street. The area is thinly built: frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys face Sharp Street (numbers 418 to 436) and Lafayette Street, with a summer house and a few outbuildings, and much of block 401 is open. A strip marked no exposure runs along the slanting left side, next to the vacant land beyond. Water pipes of 4 inches run along Sharp Street, Lafayette Street and Miller Street, and a hydrant is drawn at Sharp and Miller.
notes: Drawn turned, with north to the right.
Placed from two junctions on Miller Street (helmert); modern lot lines in block 401 agree with the placement.

50 ft. Four parts: 1 Mountain Av and East Av (Crane) along the Musconetcong River (left strip and bottom); 2 Miller St / Sharp / Lafayette, turned about 90 degrees (central box); 3 Mill Pond, Mill St, Gruendyke grist mill (top); 4 Willow Grove / Maple Av, M.B. Bowers implements (right middle).

sheet-11-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 11 is the upper strip of the sheet, showing the Mill Pond on the Musconetcong River and Mill Street on the south-eastern edge of Hackettstown, at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. The Mill Pond, with an island, fills the top of the part; the river and its race leave it over a dam and run down past the F. W. Gruendyke grist mill, an old stone building with no roof on stone foundations, heated by a stove and driven by water power. Mill Street crosses the river and the race on a stone bridge and runs east across the part, crossing an overflow channel from the pond on a second stone bridge; a 10 inch water pipe from the reservoir follows it. North of Mill Street, in block 20, stands the ice house of Schuyler and Carpenter, ice dealers; block 19 lies south of the street, largely open. At the right edge are a few farm buildings, a hen house, chicken houses and a wagon house. The Warren and Morris county line is drawn through the pond and along the river. The area to the left, beyond the heavy line, is drawn on sheet 10.
notes: F. W. Gruendyke grist mill (old stone foundations, no roof) on the race below the Mill Pond dam.
Schuyler and Carpenter ice house on block 20.

Placed provisionally from one point: Mill Street / Water Street, which is on sheet 10 just beyond the part's left edge, taken 1600 px (about 200 ft, the width of Mill Street's last stretch on sheet 10) left of the part, with the scale assumed and north set from Mill Street; along Mill Street the position is uncertain by perhaps 10 to 20 m. Low confidence.

50 ft. Four parts: 1 Mountain Av and East Av (Crane) along the Musconetcong River (left strip and bottom); 2 Miller St / Sharp / Lafayette, turned about 90 degrees (central box); 3 Mill Pond, Mill St, Gruendyke grist mill (top); 4 Willow Grove / Maple Av, M.B. Bowers implements (right middle).

sheet-11-4.description: Part 4 of sheet 11 is the right middle of the sheet, between two heavy lines, showing Willow Grove Street running south from Maple Avenue in the eastern part of Hackettstown, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. A brook crosses the part from left to right. The main occupant is M. B. Bowers, plows and agricultural implements, in block 3 west of Willow Grove Street: an old foundry, brick filled, a machine shop with patterns and storage, a wood shop, a wagon shed, a wagon, fertilizer, lumber and wagon shed, a feed room, a corn crib and a chicken house, with a printed note on its watchman, heating, fuel and power. Across the street in block 20 are its office and warehouse for machine parts and carriages, and a few frame dwellings. A wedge-shaped open block numbered 13 lies between Willow Grove Street and the road to its right, and a strip marked no exposure runs down the right edge. A 6 inch water pipe runs along Willow Grove Street. Sheet 9 adjoins at the bottom.
notes: M. B. Bowers plow and agricultural implement works on block 3.
Willow Grove is Willow Grove Street in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the south-western outskirts of Hackettstown at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north lies towards the left. Washington Street runs across the top of the sheet and curves down to the upper right, where Mountain Avenue is lettered. Madison, Monroe and Jefferson Streets cross the left half, with West Plane Street at the left edge, Center Street and Warren Street as cross streets, 1st Avenue near the lower left, and Reese Avenue and Bells Lane as long roads running down the sheet at the bottom and right. The left edge holds the town's built-up fringe: a public school drawn in pink with a courtyard (block 35), a florist's greenhouse plant (A. D. Herrick), detached dwellings and a few commercial buildings. The right-hand part of the sheet is mostly open ground and large lots, crossed by faint property lines and a winding path or stream. Smith Bros. and Co. have a small works near Reese Avenue at the bottom, and a row of dwellings lines the upper right along Washington Street. Block numbers 36, 53, 57, 50, 102, 103, 106 and 405 are printed. A compass rose stands near the lower middle. Neighbouring sheets are 9 above, 10 to the right and 8 and 6 to the left.
notes: West Plane is Plane Street in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-13-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 13 is the main map of the sheet, covering the northern end of Hackettstown on both sides of Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Main Street runs down the right side of the part; Baldwin Street, Valley View Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Stiger Street cross it, and Charles Street, Vail Street and Harvey Street run between them. Blocks 406 to 418 are numbered. The district is residential and thinly built: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys on large lots, many with barns, stables and poultry houses, and much open land, with a Union Mission chapel on Main Street. The Morris Canal, with its tow path and a roadway, crosses the upper part from the left towards a basin at the top right, and Main Street crosses it on a wooden bridge; beyond it Malvin Hill Road runs along a wooded, steep hillside with a few houses and a wagon shed, and Independence Township is lettered across the land north of the borough. A proposed street is drawn north of Baldwin Street near a compass rose. Water pipes of 3 and 4 inches run along Main, Baldwin, Valley View, Prospect and Stiger, and the scale is lettered 100 feet to an inch. The heavy lines on the left enclose parts 2 and 3, and a box at the top encloses part 4.
notes: West of Main Street, Baldwin, Valley View Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Stiger are West Baldwin Street, West Valley View Avenue, West Prospect Street and West Stiger Street in OpenStreetMap; east of it they carry East.
The Morris Canal, now abandoned, crosses the part; Main Street crosses it on a wooden bridge.
Malvin Hill Road is not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-13-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 13 is the upper left of the sheet, an area east of the downtown of Hackettstown between Ruland Avenue at the top and Willow Grove Street at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Maple Avenue runs down the left side and Franklin Street down the middle, with Cook Street in the upper right; Ruland Avenue, Ashley Avenue (lettered as new) and East Plane Street cross them. Blocks 86, 219, 220, 221, 222 and 419 are numbered. Most of the part is open or thinly built, with a few frame dwellings, barns and garages along Ruland Avenue, Ashley Avenue and Franklin Street, and long vacant lots towards the left edge. The Hackettstown Sportswear Co., makers of caps, occupies a small brick building on East Plane Street near Franklin Street. At the top left a few buildings of sheet 5 appear around the label 5, and the Musconetcong River runs in at the lower left near the label 11. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Ruland Avenue, East Plane Street and Willow Grove Street, a 6 inch pipe from the reservoir enters at the right, and a strip along the slanting heavy line is marked no exposure.
notes: Ashley Avenue is lettered 'Ashley Av. (New)'; the index has 'New, see Ashley Ave.'.

sheet-13-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 13 is the lower left of the sheet, below a heavy line, showing Willow Grove Street between Franklin Street and Cook Street and beyond in the eastern part of Hackettstown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Blocks 221 and 222 lie north of Willow Grove Street, divided by Cook Street, and block 20 lies to the south. The area is almost rural: a handful of frame dwellings and barns on large lots, a large frame barn noted at a distance behind block 222, and open land marked no exposure along the bottom. A 4 inch water pipe runs along Willow Grove Street and Franklin Street, with hydrants at Franklin Street and near the east end. The scale bar of the sheet is printed at the lower right.
notes: Placed from two junctions on Willow Grove Street (helmert); low confidence.
